# AGOT Alternate World Compatch

## B-level branch workflow and release 1.11.2.8 (2026-11-11)

AAWC now uses one development branch per B-level version: the B-level identifier is the first two components of an `a.b.c.d` release, so all `1.11.x.x` development belongs on branch `1.11`. `main` is reserved for the latest verified, packaged working build and must not be repurposed as the active development branch. This release establishes `1.11` from the verified `main` commit for `1.11.2.8`; its local checkout tracks `origin/1.11`.

For a normal change, work and validate on the active B-level branch. When it is ready to release, increment both AAWC descriptors and this master, build the one current package into `release/`, run the focused checks and exact source/archive/manifest parity verification, then commit the source, package, manifest, evidence, and documentation together. Push the B-level branch and its annotated `v<a.b.c.d>` tag. Only after that verified release commit is available should it be fast-forwarded or merged into `main` and `main` pushed, leaving `main` at that exact latest working build. Git history and GitHub Releases remain the archive; local per-version folders must not return.

When beginning a future B-level line, first ensure `main` names the latest verified release, then create the new branch directly from that commit (for example, `1.12` from released `main`), publish it as `origin/1.12`, set the local upstream, and perform new development there. Never create a new B-level branch from unverified work or leave a released `main` commit absent from its corresponding B-level branch.

Release `1.11.2.8` is the branch-workflow documentation/package release. Both descriptors are `1.11.2.8`; it contains no gameplay, dependency, or Stage 2 formula change. Its package and manifest are generated from the current source and verified by the focused exact parity check recorded with this release.

## Portable development and installation paths — 1.11.2.6 (2026-11-11)

The retained release, installation, runtime-staging, log-packaging, and background-run entry points are now clone-safe. Repository locations derive from the script location through `scripts/aawc_paths.py`; no retained path-resolution script or active outer mod descriptor embeds `C:\Users\sheac` or the prior `E:\SteamLibrary` install. Both active outer descriptors use the portable Paradox transport paths `mod/AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch` and `mod/AAWC_Dependencies_Modpack`.

For an ordinary Windows CK3 profile, tools default to `%USERPROFILE%\Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III`. Set `AAWC_CK3_USER_DIR` when the profile is elsewhere. CK3 executables are intentionally not guessed: set `AAWC_CK3_EXECUTABLE` or pass `--ck3-executable`/`-Ck3Executable` to a command that launches or stages runtime work. The external AGOT/Workshop inputs used by specialized legacy validators must likewise be supplied explicitly by their command-line options; they are not required for Stage 2 package, source, or portability validation.

Fresh-clone verification is `python -X utf8 -B scripts/test_aawc_portable_paths.py`. It copies the resolver into a differently named temporary checkout, proves the repository root follows that checkout, exercises `AAWC_CK3_USER_DIR` and `AAWC_CK3_EXECUTABLE` overrides, rejects a staging request without configured CK3 before it writes anything, rejects the previous-PC absolute literals across retained entry points/descriptors, and asserts that the obsolete `versions/` layout is absent. The former `1.11.2.6` and Dependencies `1.1.2` package receipts remain historical evidence in the pre-cleanup snapshot. The current package and workflow are documented in the cleanup section above. The pending Stage 2 rendered inspection remains pending and is not certified by this portability work.

## Stage 2 Population UI living-conditions repair — 1.11.2.4 (2026-11-11)

Rendered Stillside inspection of `1.11.2.3` established a narrow presentation defect: the Population tab exposed coherent capacity totals but no player-facing Stage 2 living-condition scores or crowding relationship. Build `1.11.2.4` repairs that omission without changing the Stage 1 demographic ledger, Stage 2 condition calculations, building contributions, monthly authority, resident counts, or any Stage 3 catalogue content.

The Population tab now contains a **Living Conditions** panel bound directly to the six existing effective-condition accessors: **Sustenance, Habitation, Opportunity, Health, Security, and Amenities**. Scores render on the established 0–100 scale, with 50 identified as neutral. Each score tooltip also renders its structural baseline and explains the dimension's bounded responsibility, preserving the distinction between enduring infrastructure/geography and current resident experience. The UI does not cache or write any condition value.

The same panel now renders **Occupancy** as an uncapped percentage plus the explicit `current residents / physical capacity` relationship. Its presentation states no crowding below 80%, Habitation pressure from 80% to below 90%, Habitation and Health pressure from 90% to below 100%, and over-capacity crowding from 100% upward. The display adapter multiplies the existing read-only occupancy ratio by 100 and deliberately has no upper clamp, so settlements above nominal capacity remain truthfully visible. The thresholds mirror the existing Stage 2 pressure onsets and do not add another demographic penalty.

Focused automated validation passes **42/42**: 5/5 new Population UI data-path checks, 18/18 Stage 2 condition/capacity checks, 8/8 Stage 2 demographic-integration checks, 1/1 hospice consistency check, and 10/10 Stage 1 bounded cohort-arithmetic checks. The new UI test also compares the workspace against packaged `1.11.2.3` and proves that the only game-payload changes are the two version descriptors, `window_county_view.gui`, `aawc_population_l_english.yml`, and the read-only Stage 2 display accessor; no demographic effect/rate file or Stage 3 content changed. ## Stage 2 natural-demography integration — 1.11.2.1 (2026-11-09)

**Assigned birth/mortality contract complete: SOURCE / PROTOTYPE VERIFIED.** The existing thirteen-band Stage 1 ledger and its sole guarded monthly authority remain authoritative. No second population ledger, demographic target, hard cap, crowding deletion, or scalar target-growth calculation was introduced. This evidence does not claim native CK3 parser/runtime, save, UI, or rendered certification.

### Fertility

`aawc_reforging_cohort_candidate_monthly_births` retains the Stage 1 reproductive-civilian base (`ages 15–39 × 0.011 per month`) and now multiplies it by effective-condition factors. Habitation has the strongest deficiency response, Sustenance the next strongest, and Opportunity a smaller meaningful response. Surplus-condition gains are deliberately shallower than deficiency penalties, bounding the individual factors at Habitation `0.20–1.10`, Sustenance `0.40–1.075`, and Opportunity `0.80–1.025`. Security changes fertility only below effective score 35, with a floor of 0.65. Health has no direct birth multiplier and acts primarily through survival; Amenities has none.

At exact 50/50/50/50/50/50 effective conditions the combined multiplier is exactly 1, preserving the Stage 1 neutral baseline. A building cannot affect births except through the reusable Stage 2 effective scores, so Stage 3 can add contribution rows without editing this demographic formula.

### Age-specific ordinary mortality

All thirteen existing Stage 1 annual mortality baselines and per-band fractional carries remain unchanged. Each age-band candidate now uses a condition multiplier derived independently from effective Sustenance, Health, and Habitation. Deficiencies add distinct deprivation, illness/sanitation, and shelter/crowding risk; surpluses provide smaller bounded survival relief. Effective Security contributes only below score 25. Opportunity and Amenities are absent from ordinary mortality.

The age multipliers deliberately distinguish infant, child, young-adult, mature-adult, older-adult, and elderly vulnerability. Infants/children and residents 60+ have materially larger hardship coefficients than ages 15–39; older adults are intermediate. Multipliers are bounded at `0.45–12`, so favorable conditions cannot erase baseline mortality and extreme hardship cannot produce unbounded arithmetic.

### Capacity pressure, crises, and authority

Crowding still acts only through the already established effective Habitation and Health deductions. There is no additional direct crowding birth/death penalty. The title-transfer cadence-recovery route now refreshes dynamic structural/effective inputs before its guarded tick, matching the normal monthly route and preventing one stale-condition month.

Raid, siege, and occupation completion losses remain centralized in `aawc_population_apply_warfare_population_loss_effect` and `aawc_reforging_cohort_death_population_effect`, with their separate external-death carry/accounting. Active disruption can temporarily reduce effective Security/Sustenance and therefore influence ordinary demography, but the condition code and monthly authority do not repeat the event percentage. Epidemics continue to act through effective Health because no separate AAWC epidemic population debit exists.

## Stage 2 conditions and physical capacity foundation — 1.11.2.0 (2026-11-09)

**Assigned conditions/capacity contract complete: SOURCE / PROTOTYPE VERIFIED.** This is the first installable `1.11.2.x` development package, not certification of the complete Stage 2 demographic system. Birth and mortality multipliers remain neutral pending their separately assigned integration and calibration. No native CK3 execution, rendered inspection, live installation, or Stage 3 catalogue activation occurred.

### Implemented data and lifecycle

Every eligible production-ledger initialization now computes six independently persisted `aawc_stage2_structural_<dimension>` and six `aawc_stage2_effective_<dimension>` province variables: `sustenance`, `habitation`, `opportunity`, `health`, `security`, `amenities`. Each score is clamped to 0–100. The unmodified baseline is 50; holding-type offsets are modest (40–60 in the unbuilt, neutral-geography fixtures). Read-only `<variable>_value` accessors return 50 before initialization. The existing `aawc_reforging_stage2_<dimension>_input` values now expose the **effective** scores; `capacity_pressure_input` exposes the occupancy ratio (1.25 means 125%). These inputs no longer have Stage 1's zero semantics. The thirteen age bands, carries, centralized external-loss adapters, and sole guarded monthly authority are preserved.

Structural refresh starts from 50 and independently adds holding-type, highest main-building level, county development, terrain, installed-building, and existing regional-blocker contributions. Main development adds Habitation (3 per additional main level; 0.12 per development point), Opportunity (1 per additional main level; 0.08 per development), and modest Health (0.04 per development); county development is bounded 0–100. Existing main-line base capacity and its development factor remain the size baseline. Nomad, herder, temple-citadel and pirate-den fallbacks, plus monastery/temple-citadel/pirate main levels, are now covered.

`aawc_population_refresh_holding_static_effect` computes structural conditions **before** capacity. Existing building-completion dirty flags still work. Holding type, main level and terrain have a cheap environment signature, and development retains its own snapshot, so conversions invalidate cached conditions immediately on dynamic refresh. The ordinary monthly visit deliberately rebuilds structure once to catch demolition and environmental changes lacking complete invalidation hooks. This bounded scan is a correctness choice; no world-performance certification is claimed. Effective conditions refresh before the demographic tick and again afterward. Production initialization also covers receipt-backed colonies; ineligible-ledger cleanup removes the new derived state. Display/cache refresh never initializes or changes residents.

### Existing-infrastructure mapping and Stage 3 interface

[Contribution table](../workspace/AAWC_REFORGING_STAGE2_BUILDING_CONTRIBUTIONS.csv) maps **666 concrete levels in 141 chains**, using supported `has_building` predicates across the current CK3, AGOT, Dependencies and AAWC stack. Every referenced table ID was checked against effective source definitions, including AAWC's late building overrides. Highest installed level wins within a chain; distinct chains add. The current source does not implement the Stage 3 catalogue or modify building definitions.

Purpose-specific examples: farms add Sustenance and modest Opportunity; longhouses/construction infrastructure add Habitation and settlement space; hospices add Health without capacity; guild halls add Opportunity and modest Amenities without capacity; water infrastructure supports necessities and sanitation; military facilities trade civilian Habitation/space for Security and livelihoods; extraction/manufacturing trade Health and sometimes space for Opportunity. Duchy glass gardens supply food and care resilience; the Citadel supplies care/education; Dependencies ports, mines, barracks and libraries have corresponding targeted effects. Existing regional-blocker category flags separately represent food deprivation, collapsed accommodation, poisoned ground, infestations, predators, and restricted space. Unreviewed unique buildings receive no guessed universal bonus.

The reusable province-scope `aawc_stage2_add_contribution_effect` takes **SUSTENANCE, HABITATION, OPPORTUNITY, HEALTH, SECURITY, AMENITIES, SPACE_PERCENT** (all required; use 0 for unrelated inputs). It runs only within a structural rebuild, before final clamping. Stage 3 authors add exact ID/chain/level/contribution rows to the CSV and run `python -X utf8 -B scripts/generate_aawc_stage2_conditions.py`; `--check --audit-sources` checks generated parity and source IDs. Future mappings use the same adapter without changing demographic formulas. Direct one-time increments in a building completion hook would be reset at the next rebuild and are not the interface. Contributions model installed physical infrastructure; owner/faith-dependent income-enablement predicates do not remove its structural footprint.

### Physical capacity and progressive pressure

The compatibility `aawc_population_expected` still means **physical holding capacity**. Its replacement is:

`round(max(1, main_line_with_development × (0.25 + 0.012×structural_Habitation + 0.003×structural_Sustenance) × geographic_space × max(0.25, 1 + explicit_space_percent/100)))`

Ineligible holdings return zero. At neutral 50/50 conditions, the condition factor is 1. A Habitation point has four times the capacity weight of a Sustenance point. Health, Opportunity, Security and Amenities never enter this formula. Geography distinguishes urban/fertile/open space from hills/forests, wetlands, mountains, deserts and frozen terrain. Explicit infrastructure land-use adjustments can be negative. Legacy debug main capacity plus the renamed-in-meaning **net capacity adjustment** still sums exactly to capacity, including negative adjustments. Existing migration receive limits, settlement gates, reservation/MAA consumers and county caches retain their existing compatibility variable. Explicit tribal conversion still applies its established 50% conversion rule and class-7 accounting; that is not an ordinary crowding loss.

Let `r = authoritative_band_sum / physical_capacity`. Effective Habitation loses `min(100, 30x + 400x²)`, with `x = clamp(r−0.80, 0, 1)`. Effective Health loses `min(100, 30y + 100y²)`, with `y = clamp(r−0.90, 0, 1)`. Losses at 60/100/110/125% occupancy are respectively housing **0/22/45/94.5** and health **0/4/10/22.75**. At 125%, perfect structure therefore becomes Habitation 5.5 / Health 77.25. Other dimensions do not receive crowding penalties. Scores are bounded; occupancy and residents are not capped. Even 1,000% occupancy leaves every resident untouched by condition refresh. The legacy stepwise occupancy multiplier is retired to 1; no second direct crowding fertility/death penalty exists.

Effective Security also reflects county control and active raid/siege suppression markers. Raid/siege disruption modestly reduces effective Sustenance; external event-death percentages remain exclusively in their existing ledger adapter. Epidemic intensity reduces effective Health by 15/30/45 for minor/major/apocalyptic disease. Structural scores recover unchanged when temporary disruption ends. These are environmental inputs, not new crisis-death writes.

## 1. Purpose

This document is the <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>living handoff</strong></span> for the CK3 compatch project. It must let a future chat resume work without re-deriving the project structure, patching rules, version history, workflow limits, testing expectations, or failure history from scratch.

This document should not be collapsed into a short summary. It is both an operating manual and a memory of what has already been tried, what is considered <span style="background-color:#E6F4EA; color:#24352A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>safe</strong></span>, what is considered <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>risky</strong></span>, what is currently broken, and how future patches should be packaged and documented. The current-state summary in [Section 2](#2-current-patch-state), the workflow rules in [Section 3](#3-administrative-rules-and-future-chat-workflow), the bug record in [Section 7](#7-bugs-crashes-and-risk-history), and the revision history in [Section 8](#8-version-log) are meant to work together.

## 2. Current Patch State

### 2.1 Project Snapshot

Project name: `AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch`.

Project goal: <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>preserve true LoV ruin and wilderness gameplay inside an AW-equalized world</strong></span>: tribalized, shattered, and stripped of normal building advantage.

Accepted proof case: <span style="background-color:#E6F4EA; color:#24352A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Winterfell</strong></span> remains the authoritative RH reference implementation. The broader map follows the same restoration concept: ruined wrapper stage, maintenance wrapper stage, then the restored landmark chain. For the exact wrapper rules that future chats should apply to that model, see [Section 5.2](#52-authoritative-wrapper-modifier-rules).

### 2.4 Hand-Authored Regional Blocker Description Migration

The released `1.10.5.20` description pipeline was mechanically complete but authorially inadequate. Its `scripts/generate_aawc_regional_blocker_content.py` called `root_description()` or `stage_description()` for each manifest record; those prose-composition functions have now been removed from development source, while the released runtime files remain unchanged. Root prose combines one chain motif/incident, one of four `SEVERITY_TEXT` fragments, one of 20 category scenes, and one regional-detail string. Paid-stage prose combines one of 11 `PHASE_SCENES`, one of 20 category actions, and the same regional-detail string. The 1,920-row catalogue does not contain stage descriptions.

The resulting inventory is exact: `AAWC_BLOCKER_REGIONAL_IMPLEMENTATION_MANIFEST.csv` contains 8,640 definitions, comprising 1,920 roots and 6,720 paid stages. The runtime localization contains 51,859 keys: 51,840 blocker aliases (six name/description aliases per definition) plus 19 shared effect/cost keys. Every canonical description key exists, but only 7,200 distinct description texts exist. All 1,920 root strings are textually unique only because the chain identity is substituted into the root formula. The 6,720 paid stages contain only 5,280 distinct texts; the generic `Finish the Clearance` description repeats across all four severities for each of the 480 region/category pairs, producing 1,440 duplicate paid-stage entries beyond the first copy.

The replacement prose authority is `workspace/AAWC_REGIONAL_BLOCKER_DESCRIPTIONS/`, split into 24 UTF-8 regional CSV files with exactly 360 records each. Together they must provide one row for every manifest `stage_id`, using the review columns `stage_id`, `root_id`, `stage_index`, `stage_count`, `region`, `category`, `severity`, `chain_name`, `stage_name`, and `description`. Context columns are checked against the catalogue, manifest, and stage plan; `description` is written directly and is never generated. A script may create blank scaffolding, validate it, escape it for CK3, and copy the finished prose into the three established description aliases, but it may not draft, assemble, paraphrase, or expand any prose.

Each root must establish the particular blocker and its local danger. Each paid stage must describe the blocker in its changed state, the challenge that still remains, and the concrete effort required to advance or finish the clearance. Lore should come from the actual feature, history, custom, landscape, or legend named by that chain, not from a generic region summary attached to reusable language. Keep detailed population accounting in the wiki and retain the existing concise card-length target.

Before authored descriptions are emitted, the content tool must load and validate the complete corpus and fail without writing output on any missing, extra, duplicate, empty, or context-mismatched record. The validator must additionally reject exact duplicate canonical descriptions, residue from the present severity/phase/category templates, malformed CK3 localization escaping, disagreement among the three description aliases, and any catalogue/manifest ID drift. The exact-text loader now replaces `SEVERITY_TEXT`, `PHASE_SCENES`, `root_description`, `stage_description`, and the category `scene`/`action` prose fragments in the runtime generator. They were removed before corpus completion to prevent accidental regeneration of rejected copy. This fail-closed gate was satisfied by the complete corpus before the `1.10.5.21` regeneration and build. Mechanics, names, costs, modifiers, icons, placement, and population behavior remain generator-owned and unchanged.

### Description migration implementation checkpoint (2026-10-14; released in 1.10.5.21)

### Living-human blocker removal pass (2026-10-14; source/runtime migration complete, release pending)

The empty-humanity decision rule is chain-wide: redesign a chain when a living person or organized present-day human activity creates, maintains, controls, or enforces its obstruction. References to dead history, abandoned structures, corpses, revenants, monsters, supernatural forces, and impersonal environmental or ruin hazards are valid. References to the player's clearance expedition do not make that expedition the blocker. The review is by complete chain, including every paid stage, rather than by isolated keyword hits.

All 1,920 chains were classified across the complete 24-region × 20-category × 4-severity catalogue. The affected set is exactly 240 chains: the 192 chains occupying the original `occupation_mutiny_siege` and `raiders_slavers_outlaws` catalogue slots, all 24 standard-severity `caves_mines_underways` / `occupied lower gallery` chains, and all 24 standard-severity `coasts_wrecks_storms` / `raided landing` chains. The other 1,680 chains have nonhuman or impersonal active obstacles under the rule. Historical human labels do not by themselves make a chain affected; for example, a `toll-chain crossing` is an unattended broken chain in the water, while a living toll keeper would be disallowed.

The replacement migration is complete. `awakened_constructs_relics` now occupies the former raider/outlaw slot and `elemental_rifts_manifestations` the former occupation/siege slot. Their 192 chains have new nonhuman regional motifs, four severity incidents, visible category labels, generated category flags, and dedicated construct/elemental icon pairs. The 48 standard `occupied lower gallery` and `raided landing` chains use revenants, creatures, spirits, or other nonliving obstacles without changing their category mechanics. All 1,056 affected stage records across those 240 chains were revised; the other 7,584 authored records remain outside the redesign scope.

Save compatibility is explicit rather than inferred: the replacement catalogue retains the former `raiders_slavers_outlaws` and `occupation_mutiny_siege` strings only in its internal legacy `flavour_key` values and the 192 root IDs plus 672 paid-stage IDs derived from them. Those 864 serialized identifiers are unchanged from `1.10.5.21`, while visible chain/category semantics, flags, localization, and icons are new. `scripts/validate_aawc_empty_humanity_migration.py` compares every generated building definition to the `.21` archive after masking only the intended category-flag and icon changes; all costs, modifiers, construction times, next-stage links, constructibility rules, and lifecycle mechanics match.

Validation passes at 8,640/8,640 with zero source errors, all 20 description regressions, all 1,920 catalogue chains, 1,920 roots plus 6,720 paid levels, 51,859 unique localization keys, 40 icon references, all four holding registrations, the regional lifecycle contract, settlement-completion contract, and Age of Silence contract. A second runtime generation is byte-idempotent across all eight generated outputs. The retired human-coded category identities and old icon assets are absent from visible/generated semantics; fail-closed validators reject their return. The temporary migration helper, temporary corpus backup, retired raider/occupation PNG/DDS assets, and disposable `scripts/__pycache__` were removed after validation. This remains unreleased development work: no archive, installation, or post-change CK3 UI/gameplay certification is claimed.

Assigned runtime-regeneration verification (2026-10-14): reran `scripts/generate_aawc_regional_blocker_content.py` twice from the final audited regional CSV corpus. Both executions emitted 1,920 roots, 6,720 paid levels, 8,640 manifest rows, and 51,859 localization entries; all eight generated outputs matched their pre-verification hashes and the second run was byte-identical to the first. `aawc_regional_blockers_l_english.yml` remains UTF-8 BOM at SHA-256 `C0C544B52EA4EB04FC56269B4D6E60CAE3345AAB13235DD815499ED5A1F17F51`. Exact-runtime validation accepted 8,640/8,640 descriptions with zero errors, proving all 25,920 CK3 description aliases match the audited source text. The regional-content, 20-test description, 1,920-chain catalogue, empty-humanity migration, blocker-progression, settlement-completion, pinned-AGOT wilderness-colonization, Age of Silence, and source-release validators all pass. The migration comparison confirms the 864 definitions in the two replacement categories preserve their `.21` runtime IDs and differ from release `1.10.5.21` only in intended category flags and icons; costs, modifiers, construction times, stage links, constructibility, placement, population lifecycle, and dependency ruin behavior remain unchanged. #### Group A authoring-method handoff and downstream verification

Group A established the downstream authoring method used for Groups B through D: keep ownership at whole-region boundaries; work in complete 18-record category families; make every root establish a concrete local obstacle; make each paid stage describe a visibly changed state plus the work still required; keep final clearance work outstanding until the last stage; preserve approved text and all metadata; transfer only complete literal prose; and run the global corpus review after each completed region so cross-file sentence or 12-word-run reuse is caught before acceptance. Later groups used these practices directly rather than rediscovering the workflow. Because Groups B-D are now complete, no separate B-D authoring tasks remain.

The final downstream audit confirms application of the handoff. All six Group C/D regions are 360/360 and preserve their approved openings. The first global Group C review exposed 17 cross-file repetition findings affecting 13 Sothoryos rows; those rows were individually rewritten in Sothoryos context and the review was rerun to zero errors. The completed corpus then passed the strict loader, all 20 description regressions, and the regional catalogue validator. This evidence validates the whole-region/category-family workflow, literal metadata-preserving transfer, and global repetition review, and it closes both the method-capture and downstream-adoption tasks. It does not validate rendered UI fit, runtime behavior, build output, or gameplay; those remain separate integration checks.

At the allocation freeze, no incomplete file appeared in more than one group: `dothraki_sea.csv`, `ibben_shivering_sea.csv`, `old_valyria_demon_road.csv`, `rhoyne_sarnor.csv`, `slavers_bay_ghiscar.csv`, `sothoryos.csv`, `stepstones_disputed_lands.csv`, `stormlands.csv`, `summer_isles.csv`, `vale_of_arryn.csv`, `westerlands.csv`, and `yi_ti_jogos_nhai.csv` were the complete remaining set. The historical blank inventory contains exactly 4,140 data records and has SHA-256 `947b7c85f98cdc54237f5e4d4a27f375001af7a2a29b577fbad74f84a9a08810`; it is a deterministic audit report only and contains no generated prose.

Each regional file followed the same review shape: 360 records, 20 categories, and four severity chains per category (18 records per category). Every root and paid stage was required to be a distinct, context-aware record with stage progression, present danger, concrete clearance work, and region-specific flavor. The read-only corpus review and all 20 regression tests were run at batch boundaries; runtime localization, build, and release work remained deferred until the source review reached 8,640/8,640 with zero errors.

`workspace/AAWC_REGIONAL_BLOCKER_DESCRIPTIONS/` contains the 24 source files. `scripts/aawc_blocker_descriptions.py` provides exact-text loading, metadata/coverage checks, normalized duplicate and retired-template rejection, manifest comparison, and localization alias/escaping verification. `--review` reports progress without approving runtime output; normal loading rejects unfinished rows. Controls, hidden Unicode separators, placeholders, pre-escaped strings, copy over 650 characters, repeated complete sentences of six or more words, and repeated normalized 12-word runs are rejected. The latter two checks prevent word-substitution templates from evading whole-description uniqueness. These checks cannot certify human authorship, literary quality, or historical accuracy; human editorial review remains necessary.

`scripts/generate_aawc_regional_blocker_content.py` now loads the whole corpus before preparing outputs and copies the accepted strings into its existing localization emitter. All old severity/phase/category description-composition fragments and functions are removed. Both the source review and regional-content validator statically verify this provenance boundary: the retired composer identifiers and category `scene`/`action` fragment keys must remain absent, the `descriptions` mapping must be assigned exactly once from `load_descriptions` and never mutated or method-processed, and every localization-emitter prose argument must be a direct lookup in that mapping. `scripts/validate_aawc_regional_blocker_content.py` also checks source/manifest/runtime agreement. `scripts/build_aawc_release.py` validates the complete source and all three runtime aliases before creating directories or archives, including for a custom workspace path. No fallback to old or synthesized descriptions is allowed.

Authoring considerations: giant encounters are territorial and linguistic disputes; weirwoods are preserved during clearance; frost-adders are presented as the catalogue's local name rather than an asserted canonical species; uncertain supernatural reports remain uncertain. Northern crannog leeches occupy wet approaches and flooded underfloors rather than eating dry grain. Barrow repairs account for burial customs, and garrison disputes can require pay, provisions, witnesses, or negotiated withdrawal. Dornish copy preserves water reserves during cistern repairs, separates beetle damage from foul food/water, accommodates river-family navigation on the Greenblood, and respects the varied custodians of Rhoynish graves. Catalogue motifs and specific incidents remain original AAWC scenario writing, not assertions of canonical events.

Validation at the allocation freeze: the 4,464 authored entries pass source context, distinct-text, residue, repeated-sentence/run, provenance-boundary, and card-length checks; all 8,640 scaffold records match the catalogue/stage plan and existing manifest. All 20 regression tests in `scripts/test_aawc_blocker_descriptions.py` pass, exercising exact punctuation through the real CK3 emitter, missing/extra files and records, duplicate IDs/prose, reused sentence/template-run detection, metadata drift, malformed CSV/UTF-8, control characters, template residue, manifest drift, exact-text generator provenance, alias mismatch/escaping, and generator/build rejection before writes. These are objective checks, not a claim that the complete migration or qualitative review is finished.

#### Non-intrusive CK3 computer-use boundary (2026-10-15)

- The user requires normal use of their visible desktop, screen, keyboard, and mouse to remain available. Do not activate/raise CK3, switch the user's apps/desktops, move their pointer, inject keys/clicks/scrolls/drags, or launch/restart/reconfigure the game as a workaround for this boundary. This supersedes the earlier activate-and-screenshot recovery instructions retained in the historical log.
- The selected current protocol is **observation-only**: read relevant process metadata, logs, source/install/save files; enumerate trusted windows; require exactly one returned CK3 window; request `sky.get_window_state` directly on that returned object without `activate_window`. Use the supported Computer Use JavaScript client for window inspection. Stop on absent/ambiguous windows, failed capture, unrelated desktop pixels, or stale/black output. Never repair passive inspection by activating the window or sending input.
- The installed `computer-use/26.924.22138/docs/api.md` explicitly states that input methods activate their target automatically; the skill describes SendInput. Therefore a window handle, accessibility element index, `set_value`, or secondary accessibility action is not evidence of background-safe input. No input method is approved for CK3 on the user's shared desktop under the current requirement. No such method was tested by sending input.
- Passive capture was demonstrated with CK3 already foreground; it is not yet certified while obscured, minimized, or on another desktop. The accessibility tree exposes only one CK3 pane. Read-only process/log inspection remains usable behind the scenes but cannot certify rendered tooltips, button gating, placement, or gameplay behavior. No acceptable autonomous background gameplay-control method is available in the exposed supported API; this is a scoped finding, not a claim that every possible CK3 automation environment is impossible.
- Later fresh-campaign/monthly/yearly/tooltip certification must retain this boundary. It may use user-driven interaction with passive observation, or a separately provisioned trusted environment whose display and input are demonstrably isolated from the user's working desktop. An isolated environment is a candidate, not an installed or validated solution. A second monitor, windowed mode, or a hidden shell process alone does not establish input isolation. Do not deploy alternate input injection/custom helper protocols or change the user's settings to bypass the restriction. Any future control capability must prove both genuine CK3 rendering and independent input before being adopted.
- Current-session reconnection evidence (2026-10-16): the unified controller is browser-only in this task and continued to return an empty inventory, but the computer-use skill's required session-bound `node_repl` successfully imported `@oai/sky`; `sky.list_apps()` and `sky.list_windows()` returned the live Windows inventory. The configured `codex-computer-use-b68a567d-537d-4472-9a72-1b917fb99109` pipe and signed `codex-computer-use-swift.exe` provider were both present. This closes the host/session discovery issue. When CK3 is open, enumerate, require exactly one returned `ck3.exe` / `Crusader Kings III` window, rehydrate only that returned object, and begin with screenshot-only `sky.get_window_state` without activation. CK3 was closed during the reconnect check, so no new CK3 capture or gameplay evidence was produced.

### 3.3 Packaging and Output Requirements

Every patch release must include a <span style="background-color:#FFF3CD; color:#3A3324; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>versioned patch archive</strong></span>. The project documentation is maintained as one living master file in `versions/`, not as a new per-version `.md` file for every release. This packaging rule is also part of the standing documentation policy described in [Section 3.4](#34-documentation-maintenance-rules) and should be reflected in the revision entry added to [Section 8](#8-version-log).

| Deliverable type | Required name |
| --- | --- |
| Patch archive | `AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch_X.Y.Z.zip` or phased build `AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch_X.Y.Z.N.zip` |
| Master project documentation | `versions/AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch_Documentation_Master.md` |

Every zip export must contain exactly two root items.

| Zip root item | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch/` | Required |
| `AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch.mod` | Required |

- Internal install names remain unversioned.
- Version numbers belong on the zip filename only. The master documentation filename is stable and overwritten each release.
- Version format convention: `X.Y.Z.N` is valid and preferred for iterative work. `Y` identifies the broader system or phase line, `Z` identifies the current topical goal inside that line, and `N` identifies literal update/test builds for that same topical goal. Archive all `X.Y.Z.N` builds under `versions/X.Y.Z/`.
- Preserve release zips after they are built.
- Build release zips from the current workspace copy. Root-level zips may be used as short-lived installer inputs, but the archived release zip in `versions/` is the durable deliverable.
- After producing a patch, refresh the live installed compatch from `workspace/AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch` and `workspace/AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch.mod`.
- After the live refresh, archive that release zip into `C:\Users\sheac\AAWC\versions\<X.Y.Z>\`. If that version folder already exists, overwrite the same zip name so the archived folder matches the current patched attempt for that version. For phased builds such as `1.9.96.1`, archive them under the base folder `versions/1.9.96/`.
- After every release, overwrite `C:\Users\sheac\AAWC\versions\AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch_Documentation_Master.md` with the current working documentation.
- Installer or deployment workflows may extract from a release zip into a temporary staging location, but should not delete the zip or unpack it directly into `C:\Users\sheac\AAWC` as a normal operating step.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Hard Packaging Rule</strong></span> Do not use PowerShell `Compress-Archive` for release zips. Build archives with explicit `/` entry paths (ZipArchive/ZipFile API) and validate roots by splitting entry names on `/` before delivery.
