## 4. Core Project Model and Preservation Rules

### 4.1 Core County Concepts

#### Ruin Holdings (RH)

Primary definition: authored landmark counties with a built special building or an intended special-building slot.

Target outcome: true LoV-style reclaimable ruins using ruin holders, ruin government, blockers, and the wrapper-to-restored landmark chain.

#### Wilderness Holdings (WH)

Target outcome: true LoV wilderness counties rather than superficial markers. Terrain, coast, island, hazard, and frontier context should drive blocker flavor.

#### Survivor Holdings (SH)

SH are the surviving pockets of civilization in Age of Reclamation. Assignment order remains RH first, SH second, WH third.

### 4.2 Locked Operating Rules

- Do not regress working behavior while adding features.
- Build from the latest safe line and keep the stable baseline label intact unless the user changes it.
- Do not disturb the AW tribalization and shattering pipeline. RH and WH work remain post-equalization systems.
- Preserve real LoV ruin, wilderness, and unknown-holder workflows rather than replacing them with fake parallel systems.
- RH, SH, and WH remain mutually exclusive whenever the selected rule mode uses all three.
- For modifier-normalization tasks, default to editing only `common/buildings/zz_aawc_generated_special_building_chains.txt` unless the user explicitly authorizes workflow or restoration-file edits.

### 4.3 Methods That Must Be Preserved

| Method | Usefulness | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authored-landmark RH list | Prevents false positives caused by startup-added generic slots. | Keep and continue using. |
| Dedicated Valyria restoration handoff | Safely handles stubborn Valyria-region wrapper handoff without broader workflow rewrites. | Keep and preserve. |
| Generated chain file-only cleanup | Fastest and safest way to normalize wrappers mapwide. | Default method for wrapper tasks. |
| Broader workflow rewrites for simple modifier cleanup | Historically high crash risk. | Avoid unless explicitly needed and authorized. |
| Continuous debug narration in logs | Lets future chats see the actual path the code followed instead of only end-state symptoms. | Keep and extend. |
| LoV-only building-removal inclusion | Closes the cleanup gap for default LoV counties by expanding the existing AW strip pass, while keeping LoV governments and title workflows untouched. | Keep and preserve. |

### 4.4 Important Cautions

- Not every negative building visible in LoV is automatically an AAWC wrapper. Some are LoV-native ruined chains and should not be misdiagnosed as partial AAWC conversions.
- The stable baseline label and the current working patch are separate concepts. `1.8.43` is the current stable baseline label for the previous static population-gating line, while `1.9.0` marks the current first implementation pass for the dynamic population overhaul.

### 4.5 Integration Layering and Contract Equivalence

- The general load and ownership order is **AGOT first, inserted mod second, AAWC last**. AGOT is the external pinned foundation. The inserted mod's retained behavior is the logical middle layer. AAWC owns only the documented final compatibility merge or conflict resolution.
- The supported launcher contains AGOT, `AAWC Dependencies Modpack`, then AAWC. The middle package declares AGOT; AAWC declares both preceding layers. The middle package owns 1,356 byte-exact same-path LoV files, three relocated byte-exact LoV textures, and 178 stable auxiliary files. AAWC owns all 69 modified LoV paths, exact `common/defines/lv_defines.txt` required by its `replace_path`, and every final conflict file.
- An exact-path override must begin with the pinned AGOT contract, receive the supported inserted-mod delta, and then receive the smallest AAWC-owned delta. AAWC must not silently erase newer AGOT callbacks or unsupported parts of an inserted mod.
- Literal equivalence applies only to each documented retained boundary. Renamed MGR identifiers, excluded CK3 1.20 Rite paths, omitted stale CaFG-AGOT bridge files, and excluded COW3/More Building++/More Building Slots systems are intentional exceptions, not claims of whole-mod equivalence.
- `workspace/AAWC_INTEGRATION_LAYERING_CONTRACT.md` and `workspace/AAWC_DEPENDENCIES_MODPACK_INTEGRATION_MANIFEST.md` are the authorities for ownership, remaps, exceptions, packaging, and unresolved runtime checks. `scripts/validate_aawc_dependencies_modpack.py` validates the independent package and `scripts/validate_aawc_integration_equivalence.py` is the cross-layer pre-testing gate.

## 5. Restoration and Wrapper Reference

### 5.1 Restoration Model and Scoring Reference

The earlier handoff locked in a <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>formal scoring and restoration framework</strong></span>. That reference is still useful for future expansion work and should stay in the document even when the active task is only wrapper cleanup. The modifier rules that operate on top of this restoration model are documented in [Section 5.2](#52-authoritative-wrapper-modifier-rules).

#### Size thresholds

| Size | Score band |
| --- | --- |
| Small ruin | 0-5 |
| Medium ruin | 6-11 |
| Large ruin | 12+ |

#### Base restoration values by ruin size

| Ruin size | Ruined -> Maintenance gold | Ruined -> Maintenance time | Maintenance -> Restored gold | Maintenance -> Restored time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Small | 250 | 2 years | 400 | 3 years |
| Medium | 500 | 3 years | 900 | 4 years |
| Large | 900 | 4 years | 1600 | 6 years |

#### Archetype multipliers

| Archetype | Multiplier |
| --- | --- |
| Fortress | x1.20 |
| Port / Trade | x1.00 |
| Scholarly | x1.05 |
| Religious | x0.95 |
| Mine / Extraction | x1.10 |
| Natural / Wonder | x1.15 |
| Generic unknown | x1.00 |

#### Final-building strength multipliers

| Strength bucket | Restored-building score | Multiplier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minor | 0-3 | x0.90 |
| Standard | 4-7 | x1.00 |
| Strong | 8-11 | x1.15 |
| Exceptional | 12+ | x1.30 |

Winterfell remains the canonical worked example for the multi-level restored chain distribution model. When a landmark has multiple restored levels after the wrapper stages, later restored levels should carry more of the total restoration burden than the first restored level.

### 5.2 Authoritative Wrapper Modifier Rules

This is the <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>locked ruleset for ruined and maintenance wrappers</strong></span>. Future chats should apply it to every wrapper chain across the map unless the user changes the rules explicitly. The historical reason these rules matter is reflected in the safer-method guidance in [Section 4.3](#43-methods-that-must-be-preserved) and the bug-risk notes in [Section 7.3](#73-confirmed-bad-methods-and-confirmed-crash-causes).

#### Stage philosophy

| Stage | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| In Ruins | A burden first and a promise second. The landmark is reclaimed but dangerous, unstable, and still actively harmful to the county. |
| Under Maintenance | A restrained burden-and-recovery step. The site should keep some softened ruin negatives while also previewing some highest-restored bonus families in diminished form. |
| Restored chain | The first stage where the landmark should begin paying off normally. If the real chain continues to level 4 or level 5, the highest restored level remains the reference point for maintenance-stage bonus families. |

#### Exact county tax penalty that must exist on every wrapper

| Stage | Small | Medium | Large | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| In Ruins | -10% | -20% | -30% | Implemented as `county_modifier tax_mult`. This is a county-income penalty, not a holder-ledger penalty. |
| Under Maintenance | -15% | -30% | -45% | Also implemented as `county_modifier tax_mult`. This is intentionally harsher than the ruined-stage holder upkeep because the stabilized site now demands organized maintenance. |

#### Hard rules

| Rule | Operational meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Remove all 0, +0, and -0 lines | Any line that contributes nothing or rounds to nothing in the UI is clutter and should be removed from ruined and maintenance wrappers. |
| Remove construction-time utility lines from wrappers | `building_construction_time` and similar wrapper-stage construction utility should not remain on ruined or maintenance stages. |
| Remove short-reign utility lines from wrappers | Do not let ruins or maintenance quietly improve short-reign handling. |
| Remove faith-conversion cost lines from wrappers | No wrapper should make conversion easier or cheaper. |
| Fix casualty direction in ruins | Ruins should increase lethality for all who fight there, not reduce friendly casualties. |
| Maintenance bonuses must exist on the highest restored level | The highest real restored level is the gate for allowed maintenance bonus families. |
| Maintenance negatives should mostly vanish except cost pressure | After stabilization, the main persistent negatives should be holder upkeep and county tax drag. |
| Maintenance keeps a partial burden-and-recovery mix | Under Maintenance should retain some softened negatives from the ruined stage at about 15%-35% of the ruined values, while also keeping some diminished positive families from the highest restored level only. |

### 5.3 Holder Upkeep Versus County Tax

- Holder upkeep lives in `character_modifier` as `monthly_income` and remains the direct gold drain on the holder.
- County tax drag lives in `county_modifier` as `tax_mult` and directly reduces the income produced inside the county.
- In Ruins should keep holder upkeep relatively light because that stage already carries many other negatives.
- Under Maintenance should usually carry the heavier total economic burden because the site is no longer merely a dangerous wreck. It is now a stabilized but expensive project that consumes county resources.

### 5.4 Allowed and Forbidden Maintenance Logic

Under Maintenance is not supposed to be a random mixture of leftovers. It is a <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>narrow stepping-stone state</strong></span>: keep the holder upkeep and county tax burden, preserve some softened ruin negatives in diminished form, and restore some diminished bonus families only when those families also exist on the highest restored level. The governing stage philosophy appears in [Section 5.2](#52-authoritative-wrapper-modifier-rules), and the specific numeric guidance is summarized in [Section 5.5](#55-maintenance-rebalance-guidance-from-16136).

| Keep on maintenance | Remove from maintenance |
| --- | --- |
| Holder `monthly_income` upkeep | Random ruin-only opinion, grandeur, or utility leftovers and invisible 0-lines |
| `county tax_mult` using the exact size table above | Construction-time, faith-conversion, short-reign, and other wrapper-only utility lines |
| Small positive highest-restored families only when the highest restored level also has those families | Positive families absent from the highest restored level |
| 1-3 softened ruin negatives, usually at 20% / 25% / 30% of ruined values for small / medium / large wrappers | Over-punishing maintenance clutter that prevents the stage from feeling like a stabilizing midpoint |

### 5.5 Maintenance Rebalance Guidance From 1.6.136

- Under Maintenance should not be only upkeep plus a few positives. It should keep some of the ruined-stage burden, but in clearly diminished form.
- The retained negatives should usually be the most structurally relevant ones: fort level, defender advantage, garrison burden, levy pressure, development drag, or comparable site-specific burdens.
- As a safe mapwide rule, the softened negative scale is approximately 20% for small wrappers, 25% for medium wrappers, and 30% for large wrappers.
- Maintenance positives must remain direct stepping stones to the highest restored level. Do not invent wrapper-only positives and do not preserve bonus families that disappear by the highest restored stage.
- Cleanup rules remain active mapwide on both wrapper stages: remove lines that render as 0, remove construction-time utility, remove short-reign utility, remove faith-conversion cost modifiers, and remove stale wrapper clutter.

| Maintenance retention reference | Small | Medium | Large |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Softened extra negative scale | About 20% of ruined value | About 25% of ruined value | About 30% of ruined value |
| County `tax_mult` | -15% | -30% | -45% |
| Usual positive rule | Keep some visible highest-restored families only | Keep some visible highest-restored families only | Keep some visible highest-restored families only |

### 5.6 Worked examples

Example A - <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>medium fortress pattern</strong></span>. In Ruins should keep the broken-fortress burden: negative fort level, negative defender advantage, garrison burden, development-growth damage, holder upkeep, and `county tax_mult = -20%`. Under Maintenance should keep the holder upkeep, keep `county tax_mult = -30%`, retain a softened structural burden such as reduced garrison or weakened defenses at roughly one quarter of the ruined value, and also keep small fort, defense, or growth bonuses because the highest restored Highpoint level really has those families.

Example B - <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>small port pattern</strong></span>. In Ruins may keep broken-port style negatives such as reduced safety and development, plus holder upkeep and `county tax_mult = -10%`. Under Maintenance should not keep arbitrary stress or conversion tricks. It should mostly be holder upkeep, `county tax_mult = -15%`, one or two softened port-burden negatives, and only the port-related stepping-stone families that actually exist on the highest restored port chain.

Example C - <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>scholarly or volcanic wrapper pattern</strong></span>. Remove wrapper-stage construction-time reduction and faith-conversion cost changes entirely. If the highest restored level really grants learning, military, or scholarship-family bonuses, maintenance may keep a smaller version of those. It may also keep one softened danger, levy, or defense penalty from the ruined stage when that helps the landmark feel unfinished without making it oppressive.

### 5.7 Milestone 4 Population System

Milestone 4 adds a <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>population-surplus gate</strong></span> for colonization/reclamation while preserving existing RH/WH expedition flows.

#### 5.7.1 Scope rules

- Only the <span style="background-color:#FFF3CD; color:#3A3324; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>top liege</strong></span> may use population for expansion.
- Non-top-liege rulers are forced to `0` for total/expected/surplus/reserved/available population.
- Population is still computed from all counties in the top-liege realm.

#### 5.7.2 Formula model

- Holding total population:
- `county.development_level * holding_weight`
- Holding weights:
- city = `300`
- temple/church = `200`
- castle/default = `100`
- tribal = `750`
- Holding expected population:
- `effective_holding_levies + (monthly_income * 300)`
- Effective holding levies:
- `building_levies * (1 + reconstructed levy_size modifiers)`, rounded.
- The reconstructed levy-size layer includes generated active building/province/county `levy_size` and terrain-specific `*_levy_size` modifiers, plus manually mirrored holder/capital/county-culture sources that CK3 shows through `Holding.GetMaxLevySize`.
- Current manually mirrored holder/capital sources:
- independent realm capital `+20%`
- high-tier vassal capital `+5%`
- warhorse outcome character modifiers (`+10%` or `+15%`, selected mutually exclusively so generic and combined horse outcomes do not stack twice)
- `torturer` trait `+10%`
- `absolute_control_perk` at `100` county control `+5%`
- Current manually mirrored county-culture sources:
- Westerlander county culture `+5%`
- Bellicose ethos `+10%`
- flat levy traditions: `tradition_only_the_strong -25%`, `tradition_strength_in_numbers +25%`, `tradition_frugal_armorsmiths +10%`, `tradition_agot_essari +10%`, `tradition_fp2_state_ransoming +10%`
- terrain levy traditions for matching province terrain: forest fighters, mountaineers, warriors of the dry, jungle warriors, agrarian, wetlanders, AGOT frozen flats, AGOT glacier, AGOT cloudforest, AGOT highlands, AGOT taiga bog, AGOT urban, and AGOT the bog. `tradition_highland_warriors` is intentionally excluded from the reconstructed levy formula after the Seven Points/Tarbeck Hall test case showed CK3's true holding tooltip did not apply it as a separate visible levy source.
- `family_first` trait `+10%`
- Holding surplus:
- `holding_total - holding_expected`
- County total:
- `county.development_level * sum(holding_weights in county)`
- County expected:
- `sum(holding monthly income * 300) + sum(holding effective_holding_levies)`
- County surplus:
- `county_total - county_expected`

#### 5.7.3 Expansion population costs

- Wilderness colonization population cost:
- `500 * barony_count_in_county` (minimum `500`)
- Ruin reclamation population cost:
- `1000 * barony_count_in_county` (minimum `1000`)

#### 5.7.4 Runtime cadence and reservation behavior

- Annual recalc:
- `common/on_action/aawc_population_on_actions.txt` runs yearly for all independent non-dummy rulers.
- Startup recalc:
- same file runs once after lobby load.
- On-demand recalc:
- `Perform a Census` decision recalculates immediately and shows current totals.
- Reservation system:
- Population cost is reserved at expedition start.
- On successful settlement handoff, reserve is consumed.
- On cancel/failure/invalid arrival path, reserve is released.
- Reserve protects against multi-expedition queue exploits that would otherwise overspend the same surplus.

#### 5.7.5 Development drain rule

- Consumed population converts to development drain points at:
- `ceil(population_spent / 1000)`
- Drain points are distributed proportionally across sub-realm counties by current development share.

#### 5.7.6 Player-facing interfaces

- County view Population tab (`window_county_view.gui`):
- Uses ECV-native tab button styling (`kECV_holding_tab_button`) and must remain visually consistent with the other ECV tabs (hover, selected highlight, icon framing).
- Must stay constrained to the ECV holding-content container using scrollbox-based layout; do not use wide freeform hboxes that spill past the right edge.
- Shows county-level breakdown:
- county development used
- counted baronies
- development weight from holding mix
- expected population components (income and levies)
- total / expected / surplus
- wilderness and ruin population costs for the viewed county
- Shows selected-holding breakdown:
- county development source value used by that holding
- holding-type weight
- expected components (income and levies)
- holding total / expected / surplus
- Census decision:
- `aawc_perform_census_decision` opens `aawc_population_event.0001` with total, expected, surplus, reserved, and available realm values.
- Census summary localization should prefer the proven `ROOT.Var('...').GetValue` pattern after the decision/effect has cached display variables on the character event root. Use `MakeScope.Var('...').GetValue` for non-root objects such as `GetPlayer` or saved county scopes.

#### 5.7.7 Integration points to preserve

- Population checks are now integrated into:
- `can_reconstruct_ruin` and `agot_can_colonize` scripted-gui validity paths.
- `lv_begin_expedition` interaction validity.
- AI colonization event `agot_colonization_events.0006` eligibility and execution branches.
- Reserve/consume/release hooks are integrated into:
- LoV travel on-actions (`lv_settlement_on_start`, `lv_settlement_on_arrival`, `lv_settlement_on_cancel`).
- Direct AGOT reclaim/colonize scripted-gui effect paths.

### 5.8 Milestone 5 Dynamic Population Growth System

Milestone 5 starts the `1.9.x` line and replaces the static "population is recalculated directly from development, income, and levies" model with a <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>dynamic holding population</strong></span> model. The guiding idea is that population should behave like people living in places: it persists, grows, shrinks, can eventually move, and is not merely recomputed from the current holding tooltip.

The previous Milestone 4 system remains useful as a stable reference for UI plumbing, expedition gating, and reserve/consume/release behavior. However, the <span style="background-color:#E6F4EA; color:#24352A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>stable baseline for that line is now `1.8.43`</strong></span>. The `1.9.x` work should not continue trying to exactly reverse-engineer CK3's internal levy count; growth should be based on the new model below.

#### 5.8.1 Scope and implementation order

- First `1.9.x` implementation target:
- initialize persistent population variables on holdings/provinces
- apply monthly population ticks using one third of the projected quarterly growth or plague-driven decline
- expose current population, expected population, projected quarterly growth rate, rating, terrain modifier, expected-population pressure, control factor, and disease override in debug UI
- preserve current colonization/reclamation population gates while changing reserve consumption to subtract from stored holding surplus instead of draining development
- Initial survivor-pocket population rule:
- every newly initialized non-ruin, non-wilderness holding starts with `100` current population
- ruin and wilderness holdings initialize at `0` current population
- the `100` value is intentionally small for the first `1.9.0` test pass because survivor pockets begin with level-1 tribal holds and growth should prove the dynamic system over time
- Do not implement immigration/emigration in the first patch. The growth subsystem must be stable and easy to inspect before people start moving between holdings.
- Migration model:
- public order/popular opinion is a county-level migration pressure. Higher `county_opinion` should eventually pull population in; lower `county_opinion` should eventually push population out. Patch `1.9.87` confirms this is county-scoped and reads it through `county_opinion`.
- population pressure is a county-level push/pull component. Counties over expected population should generate outgoing pressure; counties below expected population should generate incoming pull.
- war and raiding are hard blockers. If a county has active AAWC warfare, siege, or raid growth-suppression flags, migration in and out should be zero and the county should not be selected as a target.
- proximity is strictly adjacency. Adjacent cross-duchy and cross-realm movement is allowed, but a same-duchy county that is not directly adjacent is not eligible. The old `1.9.87` same-duchy target-count diagnostic is obsolete and must be removed during `1.10.5.x`; actual movement already traverses `every_neighboring_county` only.
- culture and faith determine whether an adjacent target is eligible. In peacetime, either the moving county's majority faith or majority culture must match the target county. A county whose holder is at war may flee to a target that matches neither, but a peaceful county may not migrate into a realm at war; war-to-war escape remains allowed. Kei/CaFG already aggregates its granular province populations, selects the highest-total culture and faith, and writes those identities to the county title. AAWC therefore uses the synchronized county-title `culture` and `faith` fields as the county majorities and must not repeat CaFG's expensive list scan.
- colonization should move people from source holdings to a new settlement, reclamation should move people into reclaimed ruins, and emigration should subtract from one place and add to another rather than deleting population.
- reserve/consume behavior now removes people from stored holding surplus on completion; future work can refine source selection and target settlement seeding.
- Implementation order: `1.9.87` diagnostics only; `1.9.88` begins actual movement with same-county holding movement and map-wide adjacent-county rating migration; `1.9.89` adds county-majority faith/culture/war target eligibility through CaFG's synchronized county-title fields; `1.10.5.x` removes the abandoned same-duchy and direct CaFG-list diagnostics, adds building migration ratings, and makes the AI reason about the completed system.

#### 5.8.2 Holding base growth rates

Holding type provides the natural growth baseline. As of `1.9.40`, these values are treated as projected quarterly growth rates. The CK3 monthly tick applies one third of the resulting final quarterly projection. Do not divide them by `12`, convert them from yearly values, or otherwise rewrite them during implementation. Normal non-plague growth should always be positive.

Monthly population update:

```text
monthly_growth_delta = current_population * quarterly_growth_rate_value / 3
new_population = current_population + monthly_growth_delta
```

The `quarterly_growth_rate_value` must be stored as a decimal. For example, `0.15` means a projected `+15%` quarter, with roughly `+5%` of current population applied on each monthly tick before compounding effects.

| Holding type | Base quarterly growth rate | Design reason |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Settlement | `1.0%` | A newly livable or partially reclaimed place can grow, but people do not thrive until conditions improve. |
| Ruin | `0.0%` | Abandoned dummy-held places do not naturally grow until reclaimed or transformed. |
| Tribal | `15.0%` | Tribal counties often have only one holding and need high growth to represent broad rural population, less urban density, and early social structure. |
| Castle | `2.5%` | Castles are garrison and lordship centers; they support population but are not ideal growth engines. |
| Temple | `3.5%` | Religious holdings have permanent communities plus visitors, charity, and institutional stability. |
| City | `5.0%` | Cities are the best baseline growth environment because they concentrate trade, housing, services, and opportunity. |

Formula order when no disease override applies:

```text
base_growth_rate = holding_base_growth_rate
potential_growth_rate = base_growth_rate * rating_multiplier * terrain_multiplier
terrain_floor_growth_rate = max(potential_growth_rate, 0.0005)
control_adjusted_growth_rate = terrain_floor_growth_rate * county_control_factor
quarterly_growth_rate_value = control_adjusted_growth_rate * expected_population_pressure_multiplier
monthly_growth_delta = current_population * quarterly_growth_rate_value / 3
new_population = current_population + monthly_growth_delta
```

County control remains a drag on realized growth and is applied before expected-population pressure. At `0` control, a holding can realize `0%` of its non-plague growth. At `100` control, the holding realizes all of its terrain/rating-adjusted growth before expected-population pressure is applied. Negative disease growth ignores control, because plague deaths should not be prevented by good administration.

As of `1.9.43`, blockers do not apply a separate population-growth penalty. New settlement pacing is handled by the settlement holding's low `1%` base quarterly growth, county control, expected-population pressure, and disease overrides.

Normal non-plague terrain floor:

| Situation | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Terrain/rating-adjusted growth is above `0.05%` before control and expected-population pressure | Use the calculated value. |
| Terrain and rating would reduce growth to `0` or negative before control and expected-population pressure | Use `+0.05%` growth before control and expected-population pressure. |
| Low control and high overpopulation reduce growth after that floor | Allow the final growth rate to become extremely small, including `0` if control is `0`. |
| Plague is active | Ignore the positive floor and use the plague override. |

#### 5.8.3 Expected population pressure

Expected population is the holding's current practical population target. It is not the actual population. It is the amount of people the holding is expected to support given its physical settlement foundation, upgraded buildings, infrastructure, and development. The purpose of expected population is to speed growth when a holding is underpopulated and slow growth when it is already near or above what its current infrastructure can support.

Expected population should be stored separately from current population and exposed in debug UI. It should be a flat capacity total, not a percentage-derived value and not a recreation of the old income/levy expected-population formula.

```text
expected_population =
    main_holding_line_capacity * development_main_line_multiplier
    + sum(regular_building_expected_population_capacity)
    + duchy_building_expected_population_capacity
    + future_special_capacity_sources
```

Main holding line capacity is the foundation. In a normal mature holding, it should contribute at least about half of the expected population. Buildings then represent the physical expansion, infrastructure, work, food, civic institutions, and organized space that let more people live there.

Recommended first-pass main holding line anchors:

| Main holding line | Final base expected population | Development scaling | Design reason |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Ruin | `0` | None until reclaimed | No normal population target. |
| Settlement | `2,500` | `+0.45%` per development | Livable start with little surplus capacity. |
| Castle | `9,000` | `+0.45%` per development | Needs excellent capacity buildings to approach `25,000`. |
| Temple | `10,500` | `+0.45%` per development | Institutional base between castle and city. |
| Tribal | `7,300` | `+0.45%` per development | Broad rural population represented by one holding, but tuned below fresh feudal conversion so feudalization feels like an upgrade. |
| City | `13,000` | `+0.45%` per development | Best ordinary baseline for reaching `25,000+`. |

Development should increase only the main holding line's capacity in the first implementation. This rewards long-term investment without making expected population flicker with short-term income, levies, or other unstable modifiers.

```text
development_main_line_multiplier = 1 + (development * 0.0045)
```

At `100` development, the main line contributes `+45%` capacity. For example, a fully developed city main line becomes `13,000 * 1.45 = 18,850` before buildings are added.

Recommended first-pass building capacity bands:

| Capacity role | Typical final-level capacity | Intent |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Major infrastructure capacity | `3,000` to `3,600` | Waterworks, aqueduct-style support, and major carrying-capacity infrastructure. |
| Food and livelihood capacity | `2,200` to `2,800` | Food, work, and rural livelihood support. Strong capacity, but not allowed to singlehandedly replace settlement infrastructure. |
| Occupation and economy capacity | `1,700` to `2,400` | Jobs, markets, extraction, construction support, and productive space. |
| Institutional and civic capacity | `1,600` to `2,300` | Religion, education, culture, administration, healthcare, and civic support. |
| Defensive support capacity | `800` to `1,300` | Defensive space, storage, walls, and protected organization; useful but not housing-focused. |
| Military and coercive capacity | `700` to `1,200` | Barracks, camps, dragon pits, slave camps, and coercive/military organization. Still capacity, but low. |

Building capacity should be non-linear by level. Low-level buildings add modest capacity, while high-level upgrades add clearly more. The current worksheet uses a weighted level curve so an early building is useful but the completed chain matters much more.

Capacity and growth rating intentionally diverge:

- Growth rating answers: "How quickly can this holding grow?"
- Expected-population capacity answers: "How many people can this holding reasonably support?"
- A farm, watermill, or waterworks can have strong growth and strong capacity, but it should not be the only path to high capacity.
- A fortification can reduce growth while still adding some capacity through protected space, storage, roads, and organization.
- A military or coercive building can hurt growth strongly while still adding a small amount of capacity because all constructed buildings represent some organized physical footprint.

Balance targets:

| Holding pattern | Expected population target |
| --- | ---: |
| Normal fully upgraded city with `5` to `7` balanced building slots | Around `25,000` |
| Fully developed city with balanced buildings | Around `30,000+` |
| Capacity-focused city with `7+` slots, high development, and strong infrastructure/duchy support | Around `35,000` to `50,000` |
| Castle with normal mixed buildings | Usually below `25,000` |
| Castle reaching `25,000` | Requires excellent capacity-focused buildings and strong development |

Expected-population pressure should modify the projected quarterly growth rate after buildings, terrain, and control are applied. It should never directly create or delete people; it only changes how quickly the monthly tick grows the current population.

This pressure curve is a final flat multiplier with a center value of `1.00x`, a maximum emergency underpopulation bonus of `2.00x` (`+100%` growth), and a hard overpopulation stop of `0.00x` once current population reaches `125%+` of expected population. It gives devastated holdings a recovery bonus below `25%`, leaves ordinary settlement growth neutral from `25%` through `74.99%`, then increasingly suppresses growth from `75%` through `124.99%`. The upper half is intentionally steepening rather than linear so growth slows more sharply as a holding becomes meaningfully crowded.

Recommended first-pass pressure curve:

| Current population compared to expected | Pressure multiplier | Design meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `<5%` of expected | `2.00x` | Maximum emergency recovery bonus for nearly empty holdings. |
| `5%` to `9.99%` of expected | `1.80x` | Severe underpopulation bonus. |
| `10%` to `14.99%` of expected | `1.60x` | Strong underpopulation bonus. |
| `15%` to `19.99%` of expected | `1.40x` | Moderate underpopulation bonus. |
| `20%` to `24.99%` of expected | `1.20x` | Small underpopulation bonus. |
| `25%` to `74.99%` of expected | `1.00x` | Neutral pressure; expected capacity does not change growth. |
| `75%` to `79.99%` of expected | `0.99x` | Pressure begins almost invisibly as the holding fills. |
| `80%` to `84.99%` of expected | `0.96x` | Light crowding pressure. |
| `85%` to `89.99%` of expected | `0.91x` | Early slowdown. |
| `90%` to `94.99%` of expected | `0.84x` | Noticeable slowdown before capacity. |
| `95%` to `99.99%` of expected | `0.75x` | Stronger pressure near expected capacity. |
| `100%` to `104.99%` of expected | `0.64x` | Above expected capacity, growth is clearly constrained. |
| `105%` to `109.99%` of expected | `0.51x` | Roughly half-speed pressure. |
| `110%` to `114.99%` of expected | `0.36x` | Heavy crowding pressure. |
| `115%` to `119.99%` of expected | `0.19x` | Growth is close to stalling. |
| `120%` to `124.99%` of expected | `0.05x` | Trace growth remains before the hard stop. |
| `125%+` of expected | `0.00x` | Capacity is exceeded enough that non-plague growth stops. |

If expected population is `0`, unreclaimed ruins and wilderness holdings should remain at `0` normal growth. Non-ruin/non-wilderness holdings use the positive terrain floor so harsh terrain can slow growth without becoming a death mechanic.

Expected population capacity values are now consolidated in this working documentation and implemented in `common/script_values/aawc_population_values.txt`. Separate worksheet files are design artifacts only and should not be required in release packages.

#### 5.8.4 Growth rating curve

Growth rating is the main tunable layer for buildings and other local factors. Ratings are hard-capped from `-500` to `+500`. The most a rating can improve growth is `2.00x`; the most it can suppress non-disease growth is `0.10x`.

This table is the authoritative first-pass curve. It intentionally has diminishing returns in both directions. A small positive building can matter, but stacking growth support becomes increasingly expensive. Likewise, a negative military or hostile-infrastructure stack can suppress growth sharply, but cannot push normal non-disease growth below `10%` of baseline.

| Rating | Growth multiplier | Example effect on city base `5.0%` | Example effect on castle base `2.5%` |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `-500` | `0.10x` | `0.50%` | `0.25%` |
| `-400` | `0.15x` | `0.75%` | `0.38%` |
| `-300` | `0.22x` | `1.10%` | `0.55%` |
| `-220` | `0.32x` | `1.60%` | `0.80%` |
| `-150` | `0.45x` | `2.25%` | `1.13%` |
| `-100` | `0.58x` | `2.90%` | `1.45%` |
| `-65` | `0.72x` | `3.60%` | `1.80%` |
| `-35` | `0.85x` | `4.25%` | `2.13%` |
| `-15` | `0.93x` | `4.65%` | `2.33%` |
| `0` | `1.00x` | `5.00%` | `2.50%` |
| `5` | `1.10x` | `5.50%` | `2.75%` |
| `15` | `1.20x` | `6.00%` | `3.00%` |
| `40` | `1.30x` | `6.50%` | `3.25%` |
| `80` | `1.40x` | `7.00%` | `3.50%` |
| `140` | `1.50x` | `7.50%` | `3.75%` |
| `220` | `1.65x` | `8.25%` | `4.13%` |
| `320` | `1.80x` | `9.00%` | `4.50%` |
| `420` | `1.92x` | `9.60%` | `4.80%` |
| `500` | `2.00x` | `10.00%` | `5.00%` |

Implementation guidance:

- Use a piecewise scripted-value curve rather than a complicated continuous formula. The table is easier to debug, easier to tune, and less likely to produce startup parser instability.
- Store the raw rating separately from the multiplier. UI/debug should show both.
- Building ratings should usually stay modest. A normal low or mid tier economy building around `+5` should be meaningful but not decisive. Multiple strong economy and religious investments should be required to reach the high positive bands.
- Military, men-at-arms, garrison, and fortification buildings should usually apply negative rating. They represent land, labor, housing, wealth, and institutional focus being redirected away from civilian growth.

#### 5.8.5 Terrain growth modifiers

Terrain modifies the holding-type baseline before the growth-rating multiplier. These are flat terrain suitability modifiers expressed as multipliers around `1.00x`. Road variants inherit the parent terrain and then add a small road bonus.

| Terrain | Growth modifier | Multiplier | Design reason |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `urban` | `+30%` | `1.30x` | Highest concentration of housing, services, jobs, and trade. |
| `farmlands` | `+25%` | `1.25x` | Best food security and settlement expansion terrain. |
| `oasis` | `+25%` | `1.25x` | Rare high-value habitable center in otherwise harsh regions. |
| `floodplains` | `+22.5%` | `1.225x` | Highly fertile, but with some flood-management burden. |
| `hotsprings` | `+20%` | `1.20x` | Local comfort, water, visitors, and settlement attractiveness. |
| `plains` | `+10%` | `1.10x` | Easy to build, farm, travel, and settle. |
| `forest` | `+10%` | `1.10x` | Food, timber, and resources offset clearing difficulty. |
| `taiga` | `+10%` | `1.10x` | Harsh but resource-rich and livable enough for growth. |
| `steppe` | `+5%` | `1.05x` | Good mobility and pastoral capacity, but less dense agrarian growth than plains. |
| `terraced_hills` | `+5%` | `1.05x` | Productive where developed, but still constrained by slopes. |
| `hills` | `0%` | `1.00x` | Balanced: defensible and usable, but not especially growth-oriented. |
| `highlands` | `0%` | `1.00x` | Similar to hills: viable but not naturally explosive. |
| `jungle` | `-5%` | `0.95x` | Fertile but disease, clearing, and travel difficulty suppress growth. |
| `wetlands` | `-5%` | `0.95x` | Productive in places, but disease and construction problems reduce growth. |
| `drylands` | `-5%` | `0.95x` | Usable but water scarcity and unreliable agriculture hold growth below neutral. |
| `mountains` | `-10%` | `0.90x` | Limited arable land and difficult construction. |
| `cloudforest` | `-10%` | `0.90x` | Resource-rich but wet, remote, and difficult to build in. |
| `canyon` | `-15%` | `0.85x` | Constrained geography and limited settlement footprint. |
| `taiga_bog` | `-17.5%` | `0.825x` | Combines cold, waterlogged land, and poor construction conditions. |
| `the_bog` | `-20%` | `0.80x` | More hostile wetland environment with severe travel and settlement drag. |
| `desert` | `-30%` | `0.70x` | Water scarcity and heat severely constrain growth. |
| `desert_mountains` | `-35%` | `0.65x` | Combines desert scarcity with mountain constraints. |
| `frozen_flats` | `-35%` | `0.65x` | Extremely harsh climate with limited food and infrastructure. |
| `glacier` | `-40%` | `0.60x` | Near-worst natural growth environment. |
| `sea` / `coastal_sea` | N/A | N/A | Should never produce holding population growth. |

Road variants:

| Road variant | Extra modifier | Rule |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `minorroad_*` | `+2.5%` | Parent terrain modifier plus `0.025`. |
| `majorroad_*` | `+5%` | Parent terrain modifier plus `0.05`. |

Examples:

- `minorroad_forest` = forest `+10%` plus minor road `+2.5%` = `+12.5%` / `1.125x`.
- `majorroad_desert` = desert `-30%` plus major road `+5%` = `-25%` / `0.75x`.
- `majorroad_urban` = urban `+30%` plus major road `+5%` = `+35%` / `1.35x`.

Terrain penalties are normal-growth modifiers, not death mechanics. If terrain penalties combine with other non-plague modifiers in a way that would reduce normal projected quarterly growth to zero or below, the holding uses the normal minimum of `+0.05%` projected quarterly growth before the monthly one-third split.

#### 5.8.6 Blockers and settlement pacing

Blockers represent unusable, dangerous, or unsettled space, but they do not currently apply a direct population-growth penalty. Patch `1.9.42` tested an additive blocker suppression multiplier, but `1.9.43` removes it from the active formula after user testing showed the desired pacing is already mostly covered by the settlement holding type's low `1%` base quarterly growth. A settlement can grow, but one third of that quarterly projection is applied per month and the result is still shaped by control, capacity pressure, terrain, buildings, and disease.

Current rule: do not add direct negative growth amounts or blocker-specific suppression multipliers unless a later test proves settlement base growth is insufficient. Disease remains the only current negative-growth mechanic.

#### 5.8.7 Disease overrides

Disease is not a modifier to the normal formula. It is a hard override that sets the holding's projected quarterly growth to a fixed negative value, regardless of holding type, expected population, growth rating, terrain, or control. Disease is the only current mechanic that should make population growth negative. The monthly tick applies one third of the disease override just like normal projected quarterly growth.

| Disease state | Projected quarterly growth |
| --- | ---: |
| No disease | Use normal growth formula. |
| Minor plague | `-2.0%` |
| Major plague | `-6.0%` |
| Apocalyptic plague | `-8.0%` |

Implementation guidance:

- Disease should be checked before the normal growth formula.
- Disease decline should apply even at low control.
- If CK3/AGOT exposes only epidemic intensity rather than these exact tiers, create a small scripted trigger layer that maps available epidemic data into AAWC minor/major/apocalyptic categories.

Current tuning target: with monthly application of one third of the quarterly override, a holding starting at `10,000` population should usually end around `8,000-9,000` after a minor plague lasting roughly two years, `5,000-7,000` after a major plague lasting roughly two years, and `1,000-3,000` after an apocalyptic plague lasting roughly five years.

#### 5.8.8 Warfare population losses

Warfare should make population feel like people living in places, not only a passive growth counter. As of `1.9.44`, AAWC hooks CK3/AGOT army on-actions to remove population from affected holdings when raids and occupations happen. As of `1.9.45`, those hooks emit pre-limit and branch diagnostics because the first installed `1.9.44` siege-capture verification did not show the expected warfare markers.

As of `1.9.47`, active raid or siege disruption also pauses positive/non-disease growth across the entire affected county. The implementation uses explicit county variables: `aawc_population_siege_growth_suppressed` is set when a hostile army enters a held enemy province and cleared on siege completion/county occupation, while `aawc_population_raid_growth_suppressed` is set by raid start/weekly activity and cleared on raid completion. `aawc_population_update_holding_dynamic_effect` and the live growth display both clamp positive growth to `0` while either variable exists. The clamp runs before disease overrides, so plague decline still applies during wartime. As of `1.9.48`, the Growth Rate tooltip also calls `AAWC_PopulationWarfareGrowthStatus`, which displays a red player-facing explanation only while the suppression marker is present.

| Warfare event | Population loss | Target |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Raid completion | `15%` | The raided holding. |
| Siege completion against a defensible holding | `30%` | The captured castle, tribal, or settlement holding. |
| Full county occupation | `10%` | Every non-defensible holding in the occupied county. |

Defensible holdings are currently `castle_holding`, `tribal_holding`, and `settlement_holding`. Non-defensible holdings are all other held barony provinces in the county, normally cities and temples. The `10%` county-occupation loss is intentionally separate from the `30%` defensible-holding capture loss, so the county capital or other defensible siege target is not double-counted by the county-wide non-defensible pass.

Implementation notes:

- `common/on_action/aawc_population_warfare_on_actions.txt` hooks `on_raid_action_completion`, `on_siege_completion`, and `on_county_occupied`.
- The shared province-scope helper is `aawc_population_apply_warfare_population_loss_effect` in `common/scripted_effects/aawc_population_effects.txt`.
- The helper refreshes the holding population cache before loss, subtracts the requested percentage from `aawc_population_current`, clamps current population at `0`, then recalculates `aawc_population_total`, `aawc_population_expected`, and `aawc_population_surplus`.
- Debug markers use `AAWC POP 1.9.45` and should be checked in `error.log` after raid/siege tests to confirm each hook path is firing. The most important markers are `siege hook entered`, `siege hook matched defensible holding`, `warfare population loss helper entered`, and `warfare population loss applied`.
- `1.9.47` adds `AAWC POP 1.9.47 hostile army entered held enemy province; county siege growth suppression set`, `AAWC POP 1.9.47 raid started; county raid growth suppression set`, `AAWC POP 1.9.47 raid completed; county raid growth suppression cleared`, `AAWC POP 1.9.47 siege completed; county siege growth suppression cleared`, and `AAWC POP 1.9.47 non-disease growth suppressed by active county raid or siege`. These confirm the county-wide suppression marker lifecycle and the monthly growth clamp respectively.

#### 5.8.9 Building growth-rating policy

Buildings will become the largest long-term player agency layer. Each constructed building level should contribute a growth rating from `-500` to `+500`, but normal individual buildings should be far smaller than the cap. The caps exist for extreme stacked outcomes, not normal single-level effects.

Current rating direction:

| Building focus | Suggested direction | Reason |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Food, water, farms, orchards, pastures, fisheries, watermills, hunting grounds, and habitability infrastructure | Strong positive | These directly improve food supply, water access, carrying capacity, and the ability for more people to live in the holding. They should outrank generic economy buildings. |
| Religion, temples, septs, monasteries, shrines, sacred pools, godswoods, learning, prestige, civic institutions, and cultural buildings | Positive | These improve stability, visitor traffic, education, records, social cohesion, and the culture that allows people to thrive. They should usually rank below food/habitability and above simple gold/development. |
| Economy, development, markets, quarries, logging, construction support, mines, roads, and trade support | Positive | Wealth and infrastructure help growth, but they are support factors rather than the main reason population expands. Quarries are positive because they support construction and settlement capacity even when they also have side military stats. |
| Fortifications, walls, outposts, garrisons, defensive towers, and defensive infrastructure | Minor negative | Defense helps survival but constrains literal space growth and keeps people clustered near protected structures. These should usually be less negative than true military buildings. |
| Men-at-arms buildings, barracks, war camps, warrior lodges, stables, archery grounds, armories, dragon pits, slave camps, and coercive/military labor chains | Strong negative | These represent conscription, coercion, training, discipline, danger, and supply being redirected away from civilian life. |
| Special landmarks | Manual review | A landmark may be a growth engine, a military sink, or a ruin burden depending on its restored purpose. |
| Ruin, wilderness, blocker, and transition buildings | Manual review | These often represent unfinished or hostile states and should not be auto-rated from generic stats alone. |

Current final-level rating bands for regular-slot worksheet review:

| Design role | Final-level target range | Intent |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Food, water, habitability, carrying capacity | `+60` to `+75` | Strongest building-driven growth because these directly support more people. |
| Culture, religion, learning, prestige, civic life | `+45` to `+60` | People thrive around identity, institutions, learning, and social cohesion. |
| Economy, development, extraction, construction support | `+30` to `+55` | Wealth and infrastructure help growth, but generally sit below food/habitability. |
| Defensive walls, outposts, fortification | `-20` to `-40` | Useful defenses that constrain physical expansion. |
| Direct military, MAA, conscription, coercive labor | `-55` to `-75` | Active military/coercive focus that redirects people and labor away from civilian growth. |

Balance target: a few exceptional holdings should be able to approach the `+500` growth-rating cap only by stacking high-end food/habitability, culture, economy, main holding progression, duchy support, full development, full control, and other favorable conditions. Most optimized fully upgraded holdings should land closer to `+350`. The same principle applies downward: `-500` should be reachable in extreme poor-condition or over-militarized holdings, but normal defensive investment should not collapse growth by itself.

Mixed-purpose scoring rule: building chains should not be classified only by their strongest category. Each visible or intended factor should push the rating up or down, and the final rating should reflect the balance. For example, `Gold Mines` provides `Tax`, `Development`, `Raid Defense`, and `Construction`, with later levels adding `Fort Level`. The economy and construction factors make it positive, but the raid/fortification factors pull it back toward neutral. Its final level is therefore calibrated around `+15`, not a strong positive. This same principle should apply to any building that mixes economy, culture, food, defense, and military factors.

#### 5.8.10 Building effect display research

CK3 building definitions support `effect_desc = <loc key>` as a first-class way to add custom text to the normal building `Effects:` block. This is the preferred surface for AAWC population information because the same effects block is reused by the construction list, the building-chain preview, and the county building-slot hover tooltip.

The generator should read the same canonical table used by `common/script_values/aawc_population_values.txt`, create static localization lines for each growth-rated building level, and generate a late-loading building-definition overlay that adds the relevant `effect_desc`. This keeps building UI and script values synchronized while avoiding dynamic scope calls in building UI.

Post-`1.9.30` implementation plan:

- Generate a new English localization file with unique AAWC keys and a late-loading building overlay rather than editing upstream building files manually. Implemented in corrected `1.9.31` as `localization/english/aawc_population_building_effects_l_english.yml` plus `common/buildings/zzzz_aawc_population_building_effects.txt`, both generated by `scripts/generate_population_building_effects_loc.py`.
- Parse `aawc_population_holding_building_growth_rating` and `aawc_population_holding_building_expected_capacity` from `common/script_values/aawc_population_values.txt`. These script values are the authoritative per-building-level data used by the working formula and Building Capacity tooltip.
- Include every building level whose growth rating is non-zero. Also include expected-capacity information for those same levels when capacity is present, because it is a direct population effect the player should see while deciding what to build or upgrade.
- Prefer static, precomputed text such as `Population Growth Rating: +35\nExpected Population Capacity: +2,350`. Do not try to compute the selected holding's final percentage inside the building effect text; that depends on total rating, terrain, control, disease, and expected-population pressure.
- Where a levelled chain can be inferred safely, include the upgrade delta from the previous level as a generated static note, for example `Upgrade change: +4 growth rating, +300 expected capacity.` If a prior level cannot be resolved, omit the delta rather than guessing.
- Load-order source lookup should check base CK3, AGOT, Legacy of Valyria, More Game Rules, and existing AAWC building files in practical load order, then write the final AAWC overlay file. Missing building definitions should be reported in the generator output and skipped until manually reviewed.
- Preserve UTF-8 BOM on the generated `.yml` file.
- Earlier `1.9.31` description-override attempts proved that the construction list can load AAWC text, but they did not satisfy the UI goal because description overrides do not place the numbers in the shared `Effects:` block and do not consistently cover every building effect surface.
- Current `1.9.31` overwrite removes the generated description-replacement file and uses `effect_desc` instead. The generated overlay includes 595 full building definitions, each copied from the effective source definition and amended with a static AAWC population effect loc key.

Risk notes:

- Description overrides are broad and conflict-prone because they replace upstream CK3/AGOT/LoV text for every touched key.
- English can be handled first; other languages would need separate localization files or would show upstream descriptions without AAWC growth/capacity lines.
- Dynamic script values inside building effect text are not the preferred first pass because building preview surfaces do not reliably expose the selected holding/province context. Static per-level numbers are more reliable and easier to audit.
- Runtime localization indirection should stay minimal. The county GUI tooltip work showed that long chained `$AAWC_POPULATION_BCAP_LINES_##$` replacement strings can crash or fail to load. Static fully expanded description text is safer than alias chains.
- This layer should be regenerated after any rating/capacity retune. The generator should make stale effect values harder by deriving text from the same script values as the formula.

#### 5.8.11 New holding population-cost research

The next population-system feature under consideration is requiring available surplus population before a ruler can create a new castle/city/temple holding in an empty county barony. This is conceptually aligned with the existing reclamation/colonization model: a new holding should not appear unless enough people can settle there.

Research findings:

- CK3 exposes a global scripted trigger named `barony_cannot_construct_holding` in `common/scripted_triggers/00_building_requirement_triggers.txt`. Vanilla uses it to block holding construction in Sahara desert baronies. The AI budget and several decision effects already call `barony_cannot_construct_holding = no`, so overriding or extending this trigger is likely the cleanest way to add a population gate that the normal holding-construction flow respects.
- The county GUI build button uses `HoldingView.CanNewHoldingBeConstructed`, and the holding-type choices use `HoldingTypeItem.CanConstructBuilding` plus `HoldingTypeItem.GetTooltip`. Those engine-backed checks are likely downstream of the holding construction validity rules, so a script-side trigger is preferable to fragile GUI edits.
- Starting a new holding uses the engine effect `begin_create_holding = { type = ... }` or scalar forms such as `begin_create_holding = city_holding`. The new-holding construction appears to fire province construction on-actions, because `common/on_action/province_on_actions.txt` checks `has_construction_with_flag = temple/castle/city` inside `on_building_started`.
- `on_building_started`, `on_building_cancelled`, and `on_building_completed` are available province-scope callbacks. This gives AAWC a likely reservation lifecycle: reserve population when construction starts, release the reservation if cancelled, and consume the reserved population when completed.
- AAWC already has reusable character-scope effects for this lifecycle: `aawc_population_add_reserved_amount_effect`, `aawc_population_release_reserved_amount_effect`, and `aawc_population_consume_reserved_amount_effect`. These are currently used by ruin/wilderness settlement flows and should be reused rather than duplicating population accounting.
- The feature uses type-specific script values based on half of the new holding's first-level expected population capacity. This avoids making a new location appear at full capacity immediately while still requiring enough people to found a permanent settlement: castle 1500, city 2250, temple 1750, and tribal 2250 if tribal new holding construction is reached by script.

Recommended first implementation:

- `1.9.32` adds a small AAWC trigger/effect layer that computes whether the builder's top liege has enough `aawc_population_available` for the selected empty barony's new holding cost.
- `1.9.32` extends `barony_cannot_construct_holding`, preserving the vanilla Sahara block and adding an AAWC minimum-population block so AI and engine-side construction checks do not found holdings without any available surplus.
- `1.9.32` hooks `on_building_started` to reserve the new holding population cost on the paying character's top liege when `has_construction_with_flag = castle/city/temple/tribe`.
- `1.9.32` hooks `on_building_cancelled` to release that same reserved amount if the construction is cancelled.
- `1.9.32` hooks `on_building_completed` to consume the reserved amount, reduce old surplus population through the existing dynamic population spend effect, and seed the completed holding's `aawc_population_current` with the moved population amount.
- `1.9.32` adds localization explaining the missing population requirement and a narrow county-GUI enabled check for the standard castle/city/temple holding choices. If that GUI expression proves fragile, the fallback is to keep the script-side gate and remove only the GUI-specific exact type check.

Implementation caution:

- Do not spend population at construction start. Reserve it first so cancelled holding construction can refund population correctly.
- Do not gate all building construction. The hook must detect only new holding construction, likely through `has_construction_with_flag = castle/city/temple`, not ordinary buildings inside existing holdings.
- AI behavior needs attention. Because AI budget code checks `barony_cannot_construct_holding = no`, the population gate should naturally constrain AI holding creation, but the cost must not be so high that the AI can never found holdings under the dynamic population model.

#### 5.8.12 Worked growth examples

Example A - city with one modest growth-positive building:

```text
Base city growth: 5.0%
Terrain: plains +10%
Growth rating: +5 => 1.10x
Control: 100% => 1.00x
Expected population pressure: 1.00x
Final growth: 5.0% * 1.10 terrain * 1.10 rating * 1.00 control * 1.00 pressure = 6.05%
Monthly update: current_population * 1.0605
```

Example B - castle with the same modest building:

```text
Base castle growth: 2.5%
Terrain: plains +10%
Growth rating: +5 => 1.10x
Control: 100% => 1.00x
Expected population pressure: 1.75x because current population is well below expected
Final growth: 2.5% * 1.10 terrain * 1.10 rating * 1.00 control * 1.75 pressure = 5.294%
Monthly update: current_population * 1.05294
```

Example C - military-heavy castle in drylands with poor control:

```text
Base castle growth: 2.5%
Terrain: drylands -5%
Growth rating: -65 => 0.72x
Control: 60% => 0.60x
Expected population pressure: 0.20x because current population is far above expected
Blocker multiplier: 1.00x because no active blockers are present
Calculated terrain/rating/blocker growth: 2.5% * 0.95 terrain * 0.72 rating * 1.00 blockers = 1.71%
Final growth: 1.71% * 0.60 control * 0.20 pressure = 0.205%
Monthly update: current_population * 1.00205
```

Example D - plague override:

```text
Base city growth: 5.0%
Terrain: urban +30%
Growth rating: +140
Control: 100%
Expected population pressure: 2.00x
Disease: major plague
Final growth: -3.0%
Monthly update: current_population * 0.97
```

The plague example ignores all normal positive factors. That is intentional.

## 6. Testing and Diagnostics

### 6.1 General Testing Workflow

- <span style="background-color:#DCEEFF; color:#24313A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Default Diagnosis Input</strong></span> The live CK3 logs directory at `C:\Users\sheac\Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\logs`.
- <span style="background-color:#E8E4FB; color:#2F2A3A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Primary Files</strong></span> Inspect `debug.log`, `error.log`, `game.log`, and `gui_warnings.log` directly from that folder unless the user specifically provides a separate archived log set.
- <span style="background-color:#FFF3CD; color:#3A3324; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Fallback Only</strong></span> Zipped log bundles are now optional fallback inputs rather than the normal workflow.
- Preserve and extend AAWC debug narration around prescore, classification, reclaim transfer, blocker application, and wrapper handoff so the logs tell the story of the code path. The key live markers to look for are listed in [Section 6.4](#64-important-diagnostic-markers).
- Do not overreact to unrelated mod-stack noise. Prioritize compatch-touched systems first.
- `AAWC: Diagnostic Logging` controls AAWC-authored diagnostic volume without changing simulation behavior. `Summary` is the default and records pulse completion, migration completion, annual maintenance, and completed AI actions. `Verbose` restores detailed per-path and per-scope calculation traces for focused testing. `Disabled` suppresses routine AAWC messages, but CK3 parser and engine errors remain visible in the normal logs.

### 6.2 Safe Editing Workflow for Future Chats

- For wrapper cleanup, start in `common/buildings/zz_aawc_generated_special_building_chains.txt` and stay there unless the user explicitly authorizes deeper workflow edits.
- When deciding whether a maintenance bonus family is allowed, follow `next_building` all the way to the highest restored level, even if that means consulting the original AGOT or LoV building definition outside the compatch.
- When a wrapper is part of a county-specific LoV rollout and the comment does not explicitly label size, infer size from the maintained restoration cost. Safe thresholds: under 400 gold = small, 400-799 = medium, 800 and above = large.
- After every modifier pass, grep the wrapper stages specifically for forbidden keys, `effect_desc` leftovers, and zero-value clutter instead of only checking the whole file.
- Do not silently change project policy when updating this document. If a rule changes, record the new rule and say what it replaced.

### 6.3 Current RH Giveaway Test Targets

- Focus first on `c_valyria`, `c_kastaryia`, `c_hills_of_nolos`, `c_ilvonys`, and `c_oreos`. These are the same counties referenced in the active bug summary in [Section 7.1](#71-active-bug-record-rh-counties-handed-to-vassals-in-lov-space) and the `1.6.152` / `1.6.153` version entries in [Section 8](#8-version-log).
- For the current test line, look for the full sequence: startup parity markers, MGR shatter-skip markers, then LoV dummy-lobotomizer markers. The intended story is that protected RH counties stay on ruin flow through all three phases and never enter the dummy giveaway branch.
- Then test nearby LoV RH counties where the Warden had previously granted titles to vassals.
- Confirm that affected counties stay under the ruin dummy or Warden structure through startup where appropriate.
- Confirm that their county-capital holdings remain on the intended ruin or reclaim track rather than leaking into the vassalized LoV settlement path.
- Confirm that reclamation still works normally. The goal is to stop the premature Warden handoff, not to flatten or bypass the reclaim workflow.

| Marker | Meaning / desired interpretation |

| `AAWC MGR SHATTER skipping dummy holder during shattered-realms redistribution` | The dummy ruin or wilderness holder carrying protected RH counties was excluded from the generic one-county shatter pass. |

| `AAWC FLOW after_lobby after_native_lov_reassert` | The post-shatter reassert pass was executed in startup sequencing. |
| `AAWC RH REASSERT evaluating c_*` | The new native LoV hard-target reassert pass is visiting the expected counties. |
| `AAWC RH REASSERT retook protected native LoV RH county for ruin holder` | A protected county had drifted and was force-retaken for `title:c_ruins.holder`. |

### 7.4 Confirmed Non-Fatal but Recurring Noise

- Duplicate localization warnings for `aawc_generated_special_buildings_l_english.yml` are noisy but have not been treated as the direct cause of startup crashes in this line.
- Failed landed-title fetches inside `aw_compatch_milestone_1_classification_effect` are recurring validation noise. They should be cleaned for signal quality, but they are not presently the best explanation for the pre-title regressions.
- `remove_building` warnings from preclear and building-history override effects are recurring noise. They indicate unguarded building removals and should be tightened, but they are not proof of the RH giveaway bug by themselves.
- Missing icon references and orphan-event warnings should be documented and cleaned as part of general polish, but they are lower priority than live gameplay workflow errors.
- Do not treat scary parser spam as a newly introduced cause until it is checked against the last known loading log set. `1.6.145` reinforced this rule when `lv_settlement_values.txt` parser spam turned out not to be new.

### 7.5 Rules for Future Crash and Bug Debugging

- Always preserve the last known loading gameplay branch as a rollback target before attempting invasive diagnostics.
- When adding debug, prefer narration inside already-working scripted effects or existing AGOT or LoV on_action chains instead of creating new top-level engine hooks.
- If a patch is meant only to gather evidence, say so explicitly in the document and in the patch note.
- Do not mix a large behavioral rewrite and a large diagnostic rewrite in the same patch unless absolutely necessary.
- When testing RH giveaway fixes, do not bundle in unrelated cleanup such as Winterfell wrapper-name swaps, settlement-value edits, or stale-reference housekeeping unless the user explicitly authorizes a mixed-purpose patch.
- When a user reports a crash, inspect whether the logs actually stop during parser load, during `on_game_start`, during title generation, during map generation, or later from inside game. Record that distinction here.
- Keep confirmed bad methods in this section permanently unless the user explicitly asks to remove them.

### 7.6 Current Operational Takeaway

For runtime stability and behavior reference, treat <span style="background-color:#E6F4EA; color:#24352A; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>`1.8.43` as the stable Milestone 4 population-gating endpoint</strong></span> and `1.9.0-design` as the active Milestone 5 dynamic population planning state. Continue to ship narrow, testable increments with high-signal diagnostics and patch-first packaging rather than direct edits to the live installed compatch.

### 7.7 Common Implementation Pitfalls Checklist

- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>BOM and Encoding</strong></span> Ensure every newly added or rewritten `.txt` / `.yml` script file is saved as UTF-8 BOM before packaging.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Scope-Safe Script Values</strong></span> Do not use bare `development_level` in values that can run in barony scope; use `county.development_level` for county-derived calculations.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Localization Value Access</strong></span> For event-root cached values, use the proven `ROOT.Var('value_name').GetValue` pattern. For non-root data objects such as `GetPlayer` or saved county scopes, use `MakeScope.Var('value_name').GetValue`; direct `GetPlayer.Var(...)` fails localization parsing.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>GUI Tab Parity</strong></span> For ECV tab additions, use `kECV_holding_tab_button` styling instead of ad-hoc buttons to preserve hover/selected visuals.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Container-Constrained Layout</strong></span> Keep new county-tab content inside ECV scroll containers with bounded widths to prevent right-side overflow.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Mirror GUI Edits</strong></span> When touching county GUI, keep both `gui/window_county_view.gui` and `gui_folder_valyria/window_county_view.gui` aligned unless divergence is intentional and documented.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Scoped Tooltip Context</strong></span> When localization text relies on `scope:*` script values, ensure the same scope alias exists in every caller path (interaction, scripted GUI, event) or split into caller-specific loc keys.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Variable-Use Warnings</strong></span> Prefer `set_variable` when a value is later read as `var:*`; avoid patterns that static validation treats as "used but never set."
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Patch Pair Integrity</strong></span> Always ship matching `.zip` + `.md` in `C:\Users\sheac\AAWC` and verify zip root contains only `AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch/` and `AGOT_Alternate_World_Compatch.mod`.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>Zip Entry Separators</strong></span> Treat backslash (`\`) zip entries as a failed build; release archives must use forward-slash (`/`) entry paths so installer root validation succeeds.
- <span style="background-color:#FDE7EF; color:#3B2F36; padding:1px 6px; border-radius:6px;"><strong>No Compress-Archive</strong></span> Do not use PowerShell `Compress-Archive` for release packaging. Use ZipArchive/ZipFile with normalized `/` entry names and validate root items before shipping.

### 8.111 Version 1.9.0-design

- User chose to stop chasing CK3's native holding levy count and pivot to a new dynamic population model for the `1.9.x` line.
- Documentation update:
  - Set the stable line to `1.8.43`, with later `1.8.44` through `1.8.46` treated as levy-debug exploration builds rather than the new design baseline.
  - Added [Section 5.8](#58-milestone-5-dynamic-population-growth-system), defining the dynamic holding-population growth model, implementation order, holding base growth rates, growth rating curve, terrain suitability modifiers, disease overrides, building-rating policy, and worked examples.
  - Applied user terrain corrections: `wetlands = -5%`, `steppe = +5%`, and `drylands = -5%` as the current working assumption for the requested negative drylands value.
  - Updated the growth model to monthly population updates: `new_population = current_population * (1 + monthly_growth_rate_value)`.
  - Clarified that the listed holding growth values are already tuned for direct monthly use and must not be divided by `12` or converted from yearly values.

### 8.65 Version 1.8.0

- Added player-facing population visibility tools:

- County window now includes a Population tab (ECV-based layout) showing county and selected-holding population metrics plus WH/RH population costs.

- Newly selected SH counties are now lock-seeded for future passes.
- Added explicit pass-start/pass-end logs for classification flow.
- `common/scripted_effects/aawc_milestone_3_wilderness_effects.txt`
- Added preclean step to strip WH marker from SH-protected counties before WH conversion.
- WH conversion selection now explicitly excludes SH-locked counties.
- Added post-pass audit call.
- `common/scripted_effects/zz_aawc_debug_effects.txt`
- Added `aawc_debug_audit_sh_wh_integrity_effect` with anomaly logs for:
- SH-locked county carrying WH marker
- SH-locked county carrying RH marker
- SH-locked county with wilderness holding capital
- SH-locked county held by dummy or dummy-vassal chains
- `common/on_action/agot_on_actions/agot_game_start.txt`
- Added post-lobby and post-shatter startup skip guards:
- If any SH lock already exists, redundant reclassification and RH/WH conversion reruns are skipped and logged.

- `AAWC FLOW after_lobby initial reclassification skipped (existing SH lock baseline)`
- `AAWC FLOW after_lobby post_shatter reclassification skipped (existing SH lock baseline)`
- Operational expectation: SH counties should remain SH after game start, WH conversion should continue for true WH counties, and logs should immediately expose any SH/WH drift.

### 8.1 Version 1.6.163

- User report after `1.6.162`: restore prerequisite tooltip behavior looked better, but reclaim costs were collapsing into predictable `200 / 400 / 600` tiers and clicking restore did not launch expedition workflow.

  - Dynamic reclaim-cost checks were keyed to exact `*_ruined_01` building presence, so counties already in maintained-stage wrappers could miss authored AAWC cost branches and fall through to generic tier fallback logic.
  - `reconstruct_ruin` treated `aawc_county_should_use_agot_colonization_flow` counties as AGOT direct-claim flow, bypassing expedition event startup.
- Applied fixes:
  - Updated reclaim buttons in county view, dummy-titles reclaim list, and both ECV compatibility mirrors (`gui` and `gui_folder_valyria`) to execute `reconstruct_ruin` with explicit province/actor scopes.
  - Updated reclaim-cost and tooltip resolver checks in `zz_agot_ruins_override.txt` and `lv_settlement_values.txt` from exact `has_building = *_ruined_01` checks to `has_building_or_higher = *_ruined_01` so maintained wrappers map to the same authored cost values.
  - Updated `reconstruct_ruin` routing so direct AGOT claim flow applies only to pure AGOT-rule paths, while AAWC-marked counties route into `lv_settlement_event.0001` expedition planning.
  - Updated `lv_restore_ruins_tooltip_show` to always refresh `lv_restore_ruins_tooltip` for the scoped ruin county, preventing stale-context fallback during mixed reclaim UI usage.
- Operational expectation: restore buttons should remain clickable, launch expedition planning when prerequisites are met, and preserve authored per-county reclaim costs even when the ruin chain has already moved into maintained stage.

### 8.115 Version 1.9.3

- Population monthly tick scheduling:
- Replaced the yearly scheduler that queued twelve delayed monthly events with a recursive hidden monthly event scheduled per landed, non-dummy top-liege ruler.
- Startup initializes all landed, non-dummy top-lieges and schedules their first monthly tick. Each hidden monthly tick then schedules the next monthly tick for that same top-liege.
- The yearly pulse now acts only as a safety catch for top-lieges that do not have the `aawc_population_monthly_tick_scheduled` variable, such as newly independent rulers.
- This keeps AI and player population growth on the same monthly behavior while avoiding reliance on a nonexistent `monthly_global_pulse` engine on-action.
- Main-line expected population capacity:
- Main-line capacity now scales by the current main-building tier instead of using one flat value per holding type.
- Current main-line capacity table:
- Settlement: level 1 `1,000`, level 2 `1,700`, level 3 `2,500`.
- Tribal: level 1 `7,000`, level 2 `12,000`.
- Castle: level 1 `3,000`, level 2 `4,500`, level 3 `6,200`, level 4 `7,800`, level 5 `9,000`.
- Temple: level 1 `3,500`, level 2 `5,500`, level 3 `8,000`, level 4 `10,500`.
- City: level 1 `4,500`, level 2 `6,500`, level 3 `9,000`, level 4 `11,000`, level 5 `13,000`.
- Building Capacity tooltip repair:
- Replaced the single huge tooltip localization line with smaller generated localization chunks, then references those chunks from the main tooltip key.
- This preserves the intended detected-building list while avoiding the raw-key behavior seen when the key failed to load.
- Built as patch `1.9.3`; do not copy these changes into `versions/`; that directory is populated by the user's install script.
